title: Closed-loop reward-hacking auto-mitigation (v0.71.26)
description: Closed-loop reward-hacking auto-mitigation (v0.71.26). soup train --reward-hack-mitigation off|log_only|kl_control|pid_lagrangian makes a GRPO trainer detect reward hacking mid-run and self-correct instead of only halting: a bang-bang KL controller with hysteresis, a PID-Lagrangian controller (Stooke et al.), an escalation ladder (raise KL, roll back to the last-good checkpoint, early-stop with a give-up explanation), plus anti-gaming smoothing, conservative-on-disagreement voting, and bounded reward shaping. No OSS RLHF library closes this loop. Proof-of-mechanism on SmolLM2-135M; task: ppo refuses these flags since v0.76.0, so it runs on task: grpo only; scale validation tracked in issue #286.

headings.title: kl_control — reversible bang-bang controller with hysteresis
pid_lagrangian — principled control + a safety net

blocks.html:
Closed-loop reward-hacking auto-mitigation (v0.71.26)

The reward-hack and echo-trap detectors from loop hardening can halt a degenerate RL run. v0.71.26 closes the loop: the GRPO trainer now detects reward hacking mid-run and self-corrects — it raises the KL penalty, shapes the reward, rolls back to the last-good checkpoint, and only early-stops as a last resort. (v0.71.26 wired the signal buffer for PPO too. At v0.76.0 task: ppo refuses these flags before the model loads, because the trl PPO trainer this build supports takes no reward functions and the buffer was never written; see below. This feature is GRPO-only.)

We have not found an open-source RLHF library that closes the loop from detection → automatic correction → continue. The ones we checked detect, or they halt. Soup steers the run back on course. That is the whitespace this release aims at.

The one flag

The flag takes one of off, log_only, kl_control or pid_lagrangian; the example picks kl_control. It requires a reward_hack_detector (info_rm or rm_ensemble, set by the second flag above or in the config) on a grpo transformers run. The config-file equivalent is training.reward_hack_mitigation. The schema also accepts the key on task: ppo, but the PPO trainer then refuses reward_hack_detector, reward_hack_mitigation and echo_trap_enabled at setup, before any model loads (#1441); the soup train --help text for these flags still says "GRPO/PPO".

Four modes, escalating

log_only — the eyes (no control action)

Streams a per-step mitigation_log.jsonl under the run directory: raw signal, health, drop_pct, OK / WARN / HACK verdict, current β / kl_coef, reward mean/std, completion-length mean and trend, and n-gram repetition. It provably never mutates β or kl_coef — run it first to see hacking happen before you let the controller act. The log writer is cwd-contained with rotation, secret redaction, and symlink-reject-on-rotate.

kl_control — reversible bang-bang controller with hysteresis

When a multi-signal vote (InfoRM cluster-separation or RM-ensemble divergence, plus completion length_trend and n-gram repetition) stays above the trip band for a dwell window, the controller raises β (the KL coefficient) multiplicatively, clamped to [reward_hack_beta_floor, reward_hack_beta_ceil], never crossing zero. Once the signal recovers below the release band for the patience window, it relaxes β back toward the floor. Dwell + release-patience are the hysteresis that stops it flapping.

β is written to both trainer.beta and trainer.args.beta, so it takes effect on stock GRPO and Soup's GRPO variants (gspo / dapo / dr_grpo / …); the variants read trainer.beta as trl does, and fall back to args.beta for a base that exposes only the config. (The code also writes trainer.args.kl_coef for PPO, which is now unreachable because task: ppo refuses the flags.)

(Since closed in v0.76.0: the sentence above was only true for stock GRPO through v0.75.2. The variants validated grpo_beta and dropped it, so the controller moved a β that the variant loss ignored, while trl still ran the reference forward each step (#1232). From v0.76.0 every non-standard variant applies the KL penalty, so the controller's β now takes effect on them. See GRPO Plus.)

pid_lagrangian — principled control + a safety net

Replaces bang-bang with a PID-Lagrangian controller (Stooke et al. 2020, "Responsive Safety in RL via PID Lagrangian Methods"): it treats "hacking signal ≤ target" as a constraint whose Lagrange multiplier (the β / KL coefficient) is updated by a PID law with integral anti-windup and an output clamp. On persistent hacking it climbs an escalation ladder:

  1. Raise KL continuously toward the target.
  2. Roll back to the last-good RL checkpoint (requires training.rl_checkpoint_save_every_steps), dropping LR / raising β on resume.
  3. Early-stop cleanly with a plain-English give-up explanation — which signal, for how long, and what the controller tried — surfaced through soup why.

Anti-gaming hardening (any control mode)

So the controller itself can't be gamed: per-signal EMA or median smoothing, conservative-on-disagreement voting (when detectors disagree, keep KL high), a reward-distribution-drift guard (catches a policy shifting its reward distribution to fool the top/bottom split), and optional bounded reward shaping — a capped penalty on the gamed proxy (length / repetition / sentinel token) applied over the reward-function seam and always logged.

Example config

blocks.code:
# soup.yaml
base: HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M
task: grpo
data:
  train: ./prompts.jsonl
training:
  gradient_checkpointing: true            # since v0.77.0 the default false reaches TRL; true keeps the old memory
  reward_hack_detector: info_rm
  reward_hack_mitigation: pid_lagrangian  # off | log_only | kl_control | pid_lagrangian
  rl_checkpoint_save_every_steps: 50      # required by reward_hack_rollback below
  reward_hack_beta_floor: 0.02            # positive floor, so β never crosses 0
  reward_hack_beta_ceil: 1.0
  reward_hack_trip_band: 0.30             # raise β above this drop_pct
  reward_hack_release_band: 0.10          # relax β below this
  reward_hack_dwell_steps: 2              # consecutive trips before acting (hysteresis)
  reward_hack_release_patience: 3
  reward_hack_signals: ["info_rm", "length_trend"]
  reward_hack_kl_gain: 1.5                # how hard a trip raises beta
  # pid_lagrangian only. These are REFUSED at config load under any other
  # mitigation mode, so commenting out the mode rather than these keys does
  # not work: a YAML comment does not disable a key that is still set.
  reward_hack_pid_kp: 0.5
  reward_hack_pid_ki: 0.05
  reward_hack_pid_kd: 0.1
  reward_hack_signal_target: 0.15         # the setpoint the controller holds
  reward_hack_integral_clamp: 1.0         # anti-windup bound on the I term
  reward_hack_rollback: true              # enable the rollback rung
  reward_hack_rollback_patience: 3        # trips before rolling back
  reward_hack_max_recovery_attempts: 2    # then early-stop with a soup why
  # optional hardening
  reward_hack_signal_smoothing: ema       # none | ema | median
  reward_hack_conservative_on_disagreement: true

blocks.html:
The config above is the pid_lagrangian shape, because the PID tunables and reward_hack_rollback are refused at config load under kl_control rather than ignored (when set to a non-default value), and reward_hack_rollback: true separately requires rl_checkpoint_save_every_steps. For plain kl_control, keep everything down to reward_hack_kl_gain and delete the PID block.

Defaults and bounds

Setting any key below to a non-default value is refused at config load while reward_hack_mitigation is off. The example above is not a set of defaults: it sets reward_hack_pid_ki: 0.05 and reward_hack_pid_kd: 0.1, where the schema's own defaults are 0.1 and 0.05.

reward_hack_beta_ceil1.0greater than 0 and at most 1000; must be above the floor

reward_hack_release_band0.10 to 1
reward_hack_dwell_steps21 to 100000
reward_hack_release_patience31 to 100000
reward_hack_kl_gain1.5greater than 1, at most 100
reward_hack_signals[info_rm]up to three entries: the active detector (info_rm or rm_ensemble, required) plus length_trend and repetition; the default [info_rm] is refused when the detector is rm_ensemble, so set it explicitly there
reward_hack_pid_kp / _ki / _kd0.5 / 0.1 / 0.050 to 1000 each; pid_lagrangian only
reward_hack_signal_target0.150 up to but not including 1; pid_lagrangian only
reward_hack_integral_clamp1.0greater than 0, at most 1000; pid_lagrangian only

reward_hack_smoothing_window82 to 256 recent samples kept for smoothing
reward_hack_conservative_on_disagreementfalsewhen detectors disagree, use the highest signal and keep the KL penalty up
reward_hack_reward_shapingfalseneeds kl_control or pid_lagrangian (log_only only observes) and a shaping strength above 0
reward_hack_shaping_kindlengthwhich proxy the penalty targets: length, repetition or sentinel
reward_hack_shaping_strength0.00.0 to 1.0, the size of the capped penalty

Reward shaping is therefore off twice over: the switch defaults to false, and the strength defaults to 0.0, so turning on reward_hack_reward_shaping without also raising reward_hack_shaping_strength is refused rather than silently doing nothing. Every key marked pid_lagrangian only is likewise refused, when set to a non-default value, under log_only and kl_control, as the paragraph above says.

pid_lagrangian has never had a valid run (upstream #371). In the H100 gate record all three pid_lagrangian attempts crashed (at steps 6, 25 and 8), and upstream attributes those crashes to the non-finite-gradient failure filed as #342. v0.76.0 added the gradient watchdog for #342 on task: grpo, but benchmarks/ holds no pid_lagrangian run recorded after it (checked again at v0.77.0). The mechanism is implemented and the mode is selectable; its efficacy is not established. kl_control is the mode with a demonstrated mid-run rollback behind it.

Honest limitations

This is an RL feature, so it cannot ship "schema-only" — a controller that mutates training dynamics is only real if a logged run shows it working. On the maintainer's single RTX 3050 that means proof-of-mechanism only:

  • Validated on SmolLM2-135M + a synthetic length-hacking task, with all four modes live including a real mid-run rollback.
  • The mitigation is refused on task: ppo since v0.76.0, and still at v0.77.0 (task: ppo itself still runs; it refuses the reward-hack detector, the mitigation and the echo-trap flags). v0.71.26 shipped it on PPO as BETA, with the signal buffer and kl_coef mutation unit-tested, but the on-GPU proof was always GRPO-only, and the trl PPO trainer this build supports never fed the buffer (#1441). Use task: grpo for these flags.
  • Whether the loop suppresses hacking without collapsing true reward on 7B+ models with real reward models is an open, community-validatable question, tracked in issue #286. Contributors with larger GPUs (or soup train --cloud modal) can reproduce the experiments and report back.
  • reward_hack_mitigation in {kl_control, pid_lagrangian} is mutually exclusive with a DPO-style β schedule / ref_model_ema_alpha (both drive the KL / ref dynamics).
  • It is also mutually exclusive with grpo_beta: 0 (KL-free GRPO), because the controller needs a positive β to steer (#1247). The config is refused at load: grpo_beta: 0 is mutually exclusive with reward_hack_mitigation='kl_control' (the mitigation controller requires a positive beta to steer); use grpo_beta > 0 or disable mitigation.
  • info_rm needs a reward that varies on both sides of the batch median. On a two-valued reward such as reward_fn: accuracy (0 or 1), a step whose median split leaves either half constant casts no vote and logs one warning naming the cause (#1438). Through v0.75.2 a first step near 50% success recorded a phantom baseline, so a healthy later step read as a collapse and the controller could raise β, roll back or halt on a false signal; mitigation_log.jsonl from earlier runs is not comparable. On a two-valued reward use rm_ensemble or the length_trend and repetition signals. See Loop hardening.
  • Every task: grpo run now also skips non-finite optimizer steps through a gradient watchdog, whether or not a mitigation mode is set (#342); since v0.77.0 each skipped step's warning names how many parameters went non-finite and the first few of them, and trainer_state.json keeps them (nan_param_count, nan_param_names) (#2060). See GRPO Plus.

Numbers

+184 tests in tests/test_v07126.py, taking the suite to 14,788 across ~298 files.
